#Activate packages
```{r}
library("readxl")
library("ggplot2")
library("ggpubr")
library("dplyr")
library("patchwork")
library("phyloseq")
library("RColorBrewer")
library("vegan")
library("reshape2")
library("tidyverse")
```
#Import metadata
```{r}
#upload metadata as a data frame
metadata_df <-as.data.frame(read_excel("C:/Projects/Renovoderm/files/Renovoderm_metadata_clean.xlsx", na = "N/A"))

metadata_df
```

#Subset metadata
```{r}
#keep only wound samples and remove duplicates from 16S and ITS IDs
w_metadata_df <- subset(metadata_df, Swab_type == "Wound" & grepl("^LK-16S", metadata_df$Sample_id))
w_metadata_df

#keep only Visit 1 samples
V1_metadata_df <- subset(w_metadata_df, Visit =="V1")
```

#Table 1 calculations
```{r}
V1_metadata_df$preD_pH <- as.numeric(V1_metadata_df$preD_pH)
V1_metadata_df$postD_volume <- as.numeric(V1_metadata_df$postD_volume)
V1_metadata_df$postD_area <- as.numeric(V1_metadata_df$postD_area)
V1_metadata_df$BMI <- as.numeric(V1_metadata_df$BMI)
V1_metadata_df$HbA1c <- as.numeric(V1_metadata_df$HbA1c)
V1_metadata_df$Age <- as.numeric(V1_metadata_df$Age)

#calculate range, mean, standard deviation of continuous variables
Tab1 <- V1_metadata_df %>%
  summarise(
    mean(Age),
    range(Age),
    range(Wound_duration),
    mean(Wound_duration),
    range(preD_pH),
    mean(preD_pH),
    range(postD_volume),
    mean(postD_volume),
    range(postD_area),
    mean(postD_area),
    mean(BMI),
    sd(BMI),
    mean(HbA1c),
    sd(HbA1c))
Tab1

#calculate observations and percentage for levels within categorical variables
cols <- c("Sex", "Smoker", "Wagner_grade")

Tab1_cat <- map_dfr(cols, \(x) {
  V1_metadata_df %>%
    count(level = .data[[x]]) %>%
    mutate(
      variable = x,
      percent = n / sum(n) * 100
    ) %>%
    select(variable, level, n, percent)})
Tab1_cat   
```
#check normality
```{r}
#check distribution of values with histogram
w_metadata_df$preD_pH <- as.numeric(w_metadata_df$preD_pH)
hist(w_metadata_df$preD_pH)

w_metadata_df$postD_volume <- as.numeric(w_metadata_df$postD_volume)
hist(w_metadata_df$postD_volume)

#shapiro wilk test (if p value < 0.05 variable has non-normal distribution)
shapiro.test(w_metadata_df$postD_volume)

shapiro.test(w_metadata_df$preD_pH)
```

#Figure 2: Wound pH and volume 
#2A: changes in pH across visits
```{r}
#set variable numeric
w_metadata_df$preD_pH <- as.numeric(w_metadata_df$preD_pH)

#define comparisons
comparisons <- list(c("V1", "V3"), c("V1", "V5"), c("V3", "V5"))

#perform wilcox test and remove non-significant comparisons
stats <- compare_means(preD_pH~Visit, data = w_metadata_df,
                       method = "wilcox",
                       comparisons=comparisons) %>%
  filter(p<=0.05) %>%
  mutate(y.position = c(8.8, 9.2, 9.7)) #position of significant labels on ggplot

#make box plot
pH_visits <- ggplot(w_metadata_df, aes(x=Visit, y = preD_pH, fill = Visit)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_line(aes(group = Subject_id), color = "gray40")+
  geom_point(aes(fill = Visit), shape = 21, color = "black", size = 2.5)+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9))+
  stat_pvalue_manual(stats, label = "p.signif", size = 6)+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues")+
  labs(y = "Wound pH", x = "Visit") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 16), legend.text = element_text(size = 14), legend.title = element_text(size = 16)) 
  
pH_visits
```

#2B: Changes in volume across visits
```{r}
#if post-debridement volume is NA change to pre-debridement volume. Accounts for wounds that healed and were not debrided
w_metadata_df <- w_metadata_df %>%
  mutate(postD_volume = ifelse(is.na(postD_volume), preD_volume, postD_volume))
w_metadata_df

#set variable numeric
w_metadata_df$postD_volume<- as.numeric(w_metadata_df$postD_volume)

#define comparisons
comparisons <- list(c("V1", "V3"), c("V1", "V5"), c("V3", "V5"))

#perform wilcox test and remove non-significant comparisons
stats <- compare_means(postD_volume~Visit, data = w_metadata_df,
                       method = "wilcox",
                       comparisons=comparisons) %>%
  filter(p<=0.05) %>%
  mutate(y.position = c(5.5))

#make box plot
volume_visits <- ggplot(w_metadata_df, aes(x=Visit, y = postD_volume, fill = Visit)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_line(aes(group = Subject_id), color = "gray40")+
  geom_point(aes(fill = Visit), shape = 21, color = "black", size = 2.5)+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5))+
  stat_pvalue_manual(stats, label ="p.signif", size = 6)+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues")+
  labs(y = "Wound Volume (cm³)", x = "Visit") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 16), legend.text = element_text(size = 14), legend.title = element_text(size = 16)) 
  
volume_visits
```

#2C: Correlation between wound pH and volume
#determine pearson's coefficient
```{r}
#set variable to numeric
V1_metadata_df$preD_pH <- as.numeric(V1_metadata_df$preD_pH) 
V1_metadata_df$postD_volume <- as.numeric(V1_metadata_df$postD_volume) 

#shapiro-wilk normality test for pH
shapiro.test(V1_metadata_df$preD_pH)

#shapiro-wilk normality test for volume
shapiro.test(V1_metadata_df$postD_volume)

#Pearson's correlation test
cor <- cor.test(V1_metadata_df$preD_pH, V1_metadata_df$postD_volume, method = "pearson")
cor
```
#linear regression model
```{r}
#run linear regression
pH_volume_lm <- lm(preD_pH~postD_volume, data = V1_metadata_df)

#diagnostic plots
plot(pH_volume_lm)

#coefficients and anova
summary(pH_volume_lm)
anova(pH_volume_lm)
```

#plot pH and volume
```{r}
pH_volume<- ggplot(V1_metadata_df, aes(x = postD_volume, y = preD_pH)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "blue", se = FALSE) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  labs(y = "Wound pH", x = "Wound Volume (cm³)")+
  stat_cor(method = "pearson",
    aes(label = paste(..r.label.., ..p.label.., sep = "~`,`~")))+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 16), legend.text = element_text(size = 14), legend.title = element_text(size = 16))  
pH_volume
```

#Figure 3: bacterial and fungal overview
#3A: bacterial relative abundance plot
#remove low abundant features
```{r}
#extract otu table
B_clean_wound_ps <-B_ps_nr_min23000genus
B_wound_otu <- otu_table(B_clean_wound_ps)

#remove features with few counts
B_clean_wound_otu <- B_wound_otu[rowSums(B_wound_otu) > 20,]

#check number and percent of features lost  
print("wound lost features")
lost_h=nrow(otu_table(B_wound_otu))-nrow(B_clean_wound_otu)
lost_h
lost_h/nrow(B_wound_otu)*100

#check count summary to confirm proper filtering
print("wound sample count distribution")
summary(rowSums(B_clean_wound_otu))

#update phyloseq object
otu_table(B_clean_wound_ps) <- B_clean_wound_otu
```

#calculate relative abundance
```{r}
#Transform counts to relative abundance
B_ps_rel_abundance <- transform_sample_counts(B_clean_wound_ps, function(x) x*100 / sum(x))

#merge ps into df
B_ps_tab_genus_df = psmelt(B_ps_rel_abundance)
```

#Identify top abundant genera and distribution of counts
```{r}
#summarize total abundance for each genera
B_top_genus <- B_ps_tab_genus_df %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarize(TotalAbundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(TotalAbundance)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15)  #Select the top 15 genera

#create list of top 15 genera
B_top_genus_names <- B_top_genus$Genus

#order highest to lowest abundance
B_top_genus <- B_top_genus %>%
  mutate(Genus = factor(Genus, levels = Genus))

#plot overall most abundant
bacteria_plot<-ggplot(B_top_genus, aes(x=Genus, y=TotalAbundance))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +  # Rotate x-axis labels
  labs(title="Top 15 abundant bacterial genus in wound samples", x = "genus", y = "Added relative abundances")
bacteria_plot
```

```{r}
#rename genera not in the top 15 to other
```

#plot relative abundance 
```{r}
#Ensure variables are factors
B_ps_tab_genus_df$Subject_id <- factor(B_ps_tab_genus_df$Subject_id)

#set levels to visits for chronological order
B_ps_tab_genus_df$Visit <- factor(B_ps_tab_genus_df$Visit,
                                 levels = c("V1", "V3", "V5"))

  scale_fill_manual(values=B_rel_ps_Genus_colors)
Bacterial_Genus_plot
```

#3B: Bacterial Bray-Curtis NMDS plot - subject
#statistical testing: check dispersion assumption and permanova
```{r}
#transform to relative abundance
B_rel_abundance = transform_sample_counts(B_w_ps_rare_1, function(x) x*100/ sum(x))

#set variable for testing
sample_data(B_rel_abundance)$Subject_id <- as.factor(sample_data(B_rel_abundance)$Subject_id)
x = "Subject_id"

#make sure all rows have a value for column x
meta <- as(sample_data(B_rel_abundance), "data.frame")
meta_clean <- meta[!is.na(meta[[x]]), ] 
sample_data(B_rel_abundance)<-meta_clean

#calculate bray-curtis distance
bray_dist <- distance(B_rel_abundance, method = "bray")

#check dispersion assumption, if non-significant it means that the assumption of homogeniety of dispersion holds and we can proceed with permanova
dispersion_result <- vegan::betadisper(bray_dist, sample_data(B_rel_abundance)[[x]]) 

print("anova")
anova(dispersion_result)

print("TukeyHSD")
TukeyHSD(dispersion_result)

#PERMDISP - confirms dispersion assumption. Non-significant if meets the assumption.
print("PERMDISP" )
vegan::permutest(dispersion_result, permutations = 999)

#Permanova result: p-value and Rsquared value (effect size).
bray_dist <- distance(B_rel_abundance, method = "bray")
permanova_result <- vegan::adonis2(bray_dist ~ Subject_id, data = as(sample_data(B_rel_abundance), "data.frame"))
print(permanova_result)
```
#add ordination arrows between visits for each subjects
```{r}
#Run NMDS 
B_ordination_result <- ordinate(B_rel_abundance, method='NMDS', distance='bray', k=4)

#Check stress levels if >0.2 increase k. ideally <0.1
B_ordination_result$stress

#Extract NMDS coordinates
ord_df <- as.data.frame(scores(B_ordination_result, display = "sites"))
ord_df$Sample_id <- rownames(ord_df)

#extract and merge metadata information with ordination results
meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(B_rel_abundance))
meta_df$Sample_id <- rownames(meta_df)

ord_df <- ord_df %>%
  left_join(meta_df, by = "Sample_id")

#ensure visit is properly ordered
ord_df$Visit <- factor(ord_df$Visit, levels = c("V1","V3","V5"), ordered = TRUE)

#create start and end coordinates for the arrows
B_ord_arrows <- ord_df %>%
  arrange(Subject_id, Visit) %>%
  group_by(Subject_id) %>%
  mutate(
    NMDS1_end = lead(NMDS1),
    NMDS2_end = lead(NMDS2),
    Visit_end = lead(Visit)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(NMDS1_end)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

#plot nmds: changes for each subject
```{r}
#plot Axis 1 and Axis 2
BC_NMDS_subject_B<-plot_ordination(B_rel_abundance, B_ordination_result, axes=c(1,2), color=x)+
  geom_point(size=3) + 
  geom_segment(
    data = B_ord_arrows,
    aes(x = NMDS1,
        y = NMDS2,
        xend = NMDS1_end,
        yend = NMDS2_end),
        alpha = 0.6,
        arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm"), type = "closed"),
    color = "black") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#7C35B5", "#3255B8", "#7570b3","#BF2EB8","#DB3941","#F28C28", "#66a61e", "#27BBF5", "#854208", "#3A856F"))+
  labs(color="Subject ID", title = "Bacteria")+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 10), axis.title = element_text(size = 12), legend.text = element_text(size = 12), legend.title = element_text(size = 14), title = element_text(size = 14)) 
   
BC_NMDS_subject_B
```

```{r}
ord_df$Sample_id <- rownames(ord_df)

#extract and merge metadata information with ordination results
meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(F_rel_abundance))
meta_df$Sample_id <- rownames(meta_df)

ord_df <- ord_df %>%
  left_join(meta_df, by = "Sample_id")

#ensure visit is properly ordered
ord_df$Visit <- factor(ord_df$Visit, levels = c("V1","V3","V5"), ordered = TRUE)

#create start and end coordinates for the arrows
F_ord_arrows <- ord_df %>%
  arrange(Subject_id, Visit) %>%
  group_by(Subject_id) %>%
  mutate(
    NMDS1_end = lead(NMDS1),
    NMDS2_end = lead(NMDS2),
    Visit_end = lead(Visit)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(NMDS1_end)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

#Figure 4: baseline pH and wound volume

#4A: BC NMDS baseline pH
#statistical testing: check dispersion assumption and permanova
```{r}
#set variable
x = "Baseline_pH"

#make sure all rows have a value for column x
meta <- as(sample_data(B_rel_abundance), "data.frame")
meta_clean <- meta[!is.na(meta[[x]]), ] 
sample_data(B_rel_abundance)<-meta_clean

#calculate bray-curtis distance
bray_dist <- distance(B_rel_abundance, method = "bray")

#check dispersion assumption, if non-significant it means that the assumption of homogeniety of dispersion holds and we can proceed with permanova
dispersion_result <- vegan::betadisper(bray_dist, sample_data(B_rel_abundance)[[x]]) 

print("anova")
anova(dispersion_result)

print("TukeyHSD")
TukeyHSD(dispersion_result)

#PERMDISP - confirms dispersion assumption. Non-significant if meets the assumption.
print("PERMDISP" )
vegan::permutest(dispersion_result, permutations = 999)

#Permanova result: p-value and Rsquared value (effect size).
bray_dist <- distance(B_rel_abundance, method = "bray")
permanova_result <- vegan::adonis2(bray_dist ~ Baseline_pH, data = as(sample_data(B_rel_abundance), "data.frame"))
print(permanova_result)
```

#plot NMDS: baseline pH

```{r}
  geom_segment(

        xend = NMDS1_end,
        yend = NMDS2_end),
        alpha = 0.6,
        arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm"), type = "closed"),
    color = "black") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Basic" = "#5782B3", "Neutral" ="#82B357", "Acidic" = "#B35782" )) + 
  labs(color = "Baseline pH", title = "Bacteria")+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 10), axis.title = element_text(size = 12), legend.text = element_text(size = 14), legend.title = element_text(size = 14), title = element_text(size = 14))
```

#4C: Differences in alpha diversity between baseline pH groups
```{r}
#define comparisons for wilcox test
comparisons <- list(c("Acidic","Basic"), c("Acidic","Neutral"), c("Basic","Neutral"))

#perform wilcox test and remove non-significant comparisons
stats <- compare_means(Shannon~Baseline_pH, data = B_metadata_ad,
                       method = "wilcox",
                       comparisons=comparisons) %>%
  filter(p<=0.05) %>%
  mutate(y.position = c(3.9))

  theme_classic() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Basic" = "#5782B3", "Neutral" ="#82B357", "Acidic" = "#B35782" ), guide = "none") + 
  stat_pvalue_manual(stats, label = "p.signif", size = 6)+ 
  labs(fill = "Baseline pH", y = " Bacterial Shannon Index", x = "Baseline pH")+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 16), legend.text = element_text(size = 14), legend.title = element_text(size = 14))
```

#S2B: Bray-Curtis NMDS skin vs wound (fungal)
#statistical testing: check dispersion assumption and permanova
```{r}
#transform to relative abundance
F_iw_rel_abundance = transform_sample_counts(F_ps_rare_2, function(x) x*100/ sum(x))

#add sample_id column
sample_data(F_iw_rel_abundance)$Sample_id <- rownames(sample_data(F_iw_rel_abundance))

#remove outlier samples (samples skew data preventing full representation of rest of samples)
F_iw_rel_abundance <- subset_samples(F_iw_rel_abundance, !Sample_id %in% c("LK-ITS-19", "LK-ITS-29"))
                                  
#set variable
x = "Swab_type"

#make sure all rows have a value for column x
meta <- as(sample_data(F_iw_rel_abundance), "data.frame")
meta_clean <- meta[!is.na(meta[[x]]), ] 
sample_data(F_iw_rel_abundance)<-meta_clean

#calculate bray-curtis distance
bray_dist <- distance(F_iw_rel_abundance, method = "bray")

#check dispersion assumption, if non-significant it means that the assumption of homogeniety of dispersion holds and we can proceed with permanova
dispersion_result <- vegan::betadisper(bray_dist, sample_data(F_iw_rel_abundance)[[x]]) 

print("anova")
anova(dispersion_result)

print("TukeyHSD")
TukeyHSD(dispersion_result)

#PERMDISP - confirms dispersion assumption. Non-significant if meets the assumption.
print("PERMDISP" )
vegan::permutest(dispersion_result, permutations = 999)

#Permanova result: p-value and Rsquared value (effect size).
bray_dist <- distance(F_iw_rel_abundance, method = "bray")
permanova_result <- vegan::adonis2(bray_dist ~ Swab_type, data = as(sample_data(F_iw_rel_abundance), "data.frame"))
print(permanova_result)
```

```{r}
#Run NMDS

#Check stress levels if >0.2 increase k. ideally <0.1
F_iw_ordination_result$stress

#plot Axis 1 and Axis 2
BC_NMDS_swabs_F<-plot_ordination(F_iw_rel_abundance, F_iw_ordination_result, axes=c(1,2), color=x)+

BC_NMDS_swabs_F
```
